nodes.description: Patients historically grouped under types C, D, or E Niemann-Pick disease showed partial acid sphingomyelinase deficiency with moderate sphingomyelin accumulation and foamy macrophage (foam cell) infiltration of tissues and bone marrow alongside chronic neurological deterioration. Later experimental and biochemical studies demonstrated that partial acid sphingomyelinase deficiency in this historical group was often secondary to a primary defect in intracellular cholesterol esterification rather than a primary SMPD1 defect. The "type E" label has no independent molecular basis and is now obsolete, with affected individuals reclassified to ASMD or Niemann-Pick disease type C.

evidence.reference_title: Types A and B Niemann-Pick disease.
evidence.snippet: These patients presented with hepatomegaly, foamy macrophage infiltration into tissues and bone marrow, partial deficiency of ASM activity, and moderate accumulation of sphingomyelin, but also exhibited chronic and often severe neurological deterioration. They were therefore classified as having types C, D or E NPD.
